title: Article 131A — Exclusive jurisdiction of the Supreme Court as to constitutional validity of Central laws (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 131A gave the Supreme Court exclusive jurisdiction over questions of constitutional validity of Central laws and restricted High Court handling of such questions. It was inserted by the 42nd Amendment and omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977, section 4 (w.e.f. 13 April 1978), as part of the post-Emergency restoration of High Court jurisdiction.
content.glance: Art 131A omitted by 43rd Amendment 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). Exclusive SC jurisdiction over validity of Central laws removed; High Court jurisdiction restored.
content.study:
Article 131A was an Emergency-era restriction: it channelled challenges to the constitutional validity of Central laws exclusively to the Supreme Court and limited High Courts.

Omission: Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977, s. 4 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). Related 42nd Amendment insertions affecting judicial review (including 32A, 144A, 226A, 228A) were also rolled back by the 43rd Amendment package.

Living frame: High Courts under Article 226 and the Supreme Court under Articles 32/136 retain their ordinary constitutional jurisdiction subject to living text and doctrine.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 131A as a current jurisdictional bar.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Inserted by the 42nd Amendment; omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977, s. 4 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). The omission restored broader High Court competence to examine the validity of Central laws in appropriate proceedings.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Link insertion to 42nd Amendment and omission to 43rd Amendment.
2. Do not treat Article 131A as a living exclusive-jurisdiction rule.
3. For current challenges to Central laws, use Articles 226, 32 and 136 as applicable.

examples.title: Illustration — High Court challenge after omission
examples.body: A High Court in 2026 is not barred by Article 131A from considering the constitutional validity of a Central law in a properly framed Article 226 petition: Article 131A stands omitted.

misconceptions.trap: Only the Supreme Court may decide the constitutional validity of Central laws because of Article 131A.
misconceptions.correction: Article 131A was omitted by the 43rd Amendment, 1977. It is not living law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 131A?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 131A was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977, section 4 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). It is not living law. High Courts and the Supreme Court exercise jurisdiction under the living provisions of Articles 226, 32 and 136.

examTips: Group 131A with other 42nd-Amendment judicial restrictions rolled back by the 43rd Amendment (32A, 144A, 226A, 228A).
content.migrationNote: Remediated 2026-10-09: accurate 43rd Amendment omission. Case-law gate open.

notes: Omission by 43rd Amendment w.e.f. 13-4-1978 recorded from standard sources. No case holdings invented.

keyTakeaways: Exclusive SC bar on Central-law validity challenges removed.
